title: A module with perfect degree-zero complex has finite projective dimension
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, assume the derived category of R-modules exists, and let M be an R-module. If its degree-zero complex M[0] is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], then there is a natural d for which Ext_R^i(M,N) [def-pc-ext] vanishes for all R-modules N and i>d. Equivalently M has finite projective dimension. No Noetherian or nonzero hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 00O4, 00O5, 0CXE and 065R; bounded-projective model and finite-resolution arguments

proof.text: Choose a bounded complex P of finite projective modules supported in [a,b] and an isomorphism M[0]≅Q(P). Mathlib CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective makes P K-projective. Put d=max(-a,0).

For i>d and any module N, the complex L=N[0][i] is supported only in degree -i<a. Every cochain map P→L is zero: in a degree below a its source is zero; in every other degree its target is zero. Hence the homotopy-category Hom is a singleton. The K-projective comparison Qh_map_bijective identifies it with Hom_D(Q(P),Q(L)), which is therefore a singleton as well.

Transport along M[0]≅Q(P) and the shift comparison for Q to see Hom_D(M[0],N[0][i]) is a singleton. Ext.homEquiv transfers this to Ext_R^i(M,N). HasProjectiveDimensionLT.mk with bound d+1 proves the claim. The same argument covers the zero module and a positive lower support endpoint a.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00O4, 00O5, 0CXE and 065R; bounded-projective model and finite-resolution arguments; proof written using Mathlib Ext and K-projective APIs

theorem finite_projectiveDimension_of_perfect_single
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)

    ∃ d : ℕ, HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d
